excerpt: Stripe, PayPal, Gumroad, and Lemon Squeezy block creators in dozens of countries. Here is the sovereign infrastructure that works everywhere they do not.

content.text: Stripe's availability map covers 46 countries. PayPal's risk engine flags accounts from Nigeria, Ghana, Pakistan, Bangladesh, and dozens of other markets before any human review occurs. Gumroad holds payouts for up to 30 days in certain regions. Lemon Squeezy and Paddle are unavailable across most of Africa, South Asia, and Latin America. These are not temporary oversights waiting to be corrected — they are deliberate structural decisions built into conventional [[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/usdt-payment-gateways-digital-products-explained-digital-creators-18|payment]] infrastructure designed for Western banking systems. The solution is not finding a workaround inside this system. It is [[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/how-building-crypto-store-cloudflare-pages-works-how-25|How Building]] on infrastructure that does not have the problem in the first place. That means GitHub Pages or Cloudflare Pages for hosting, Cloudflare Workers or Google Apps Script for backend logic, and NOW[[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/tron-usdt-payments-digital-products-first-principles-definitive-4|COREMERCH guide to payments]] for automatic on-chain payment verification. No platform can restrict access to a store that runs under your own accounts with no dependency on any payment processor.

This post is part of the COREMERCH infrastructure series. For the complete foundation — every component, every configuration step, and the full deployment sequence — read the pillar guide: The Complete Guide to Selling Digital Products Without Stripe at https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/comparing-real-options-selling-digital-products-without-stripe-2. That guide covers the complete architecture that this post builds on.

content.text: What Each Option Actually Offers: Gumroad payhip

Traditional platforms like Gumroad and Payhip offer a range of features for digital creators to sell their products, including payment processing, product delivery, and analytics. However, these platforms often rely on Stripe or other restricted payment gateways, making them inaccessible to creators in certain countries. In contrast, sovereign commerce infrastructure providers like COREMERCH offer a more comprehensive solution, including hosting, backend logic, order storage, and automatic crypto payment verification, all without relying on restricted platforms.
How They Handle Restricted Countries

Platforms like Gumroad and Payhip often exclude creators from restricted countries due to their reliance on Stripe or other payment gateways with limited global coverage. On the other hand, sovereign commerce infrastructure providers like COREMERCH are designed to work around these restrictions, offering creators a way to sell their products and receive payments without being limited by their geographical location. This is especially important for creators in countries with strict financial regulations or those facing economic sanctions.
Payment Speed, Fees, and Real Costs

Traditional platforms often charge high fees for payment processing, and creators may have to wait several days to receive their payments. In contrast, sovereign commerce infrastructure providers like COREMERCH offer faster payment processing and lower fees, with some providers charging as little as 0.5% per transaction. Additionally, creators can receive payments in cryptocurrency, which can be more stable than traditional fiat currencies in countries with high inflation or currency fluctuations.
Sovereign commerce infrastructure offers faster payment processing and lower fees than traditional platforms.
Ownership, Automation, and Delivery

One of the key advantages of sovereign commerce infrastructure is that creators maintain full ownership and control over their stores and products. With automated payment processing and product delivery, creators can focus on producing high-quality content and building their audience. Additionally, sovereign commerce infrastructure providers like COREMERCH offer end-to-end testing and support to ensure that creators' stores are fully functional and secure before handoff.
Which Architecture to Choose Based on Your Situation

For creators in restricted countries, sovereign commerce infrastructure is often the best option due to its flexibility, security, and low costs. However, for creators who already have an established audience and are looking for a more traditional platform, Gumroad or Payhip may still be a viable option. Ultimately, the choice of architecture depends on the creator's specific needs and goals, as well as their willingness to invest time and resources into building and maintaining their own commerce infrastructure.
